title: Formula Student after lectures
subtitle: Autonomous driving, motion planning, and road trips between exam weeks.
teaser: Autonomous motion planning on ROS, workshop testing, and racing at international Grand Prix circuits alongside university studies.
description: Formula Student is the world's largest student engineering competition, bringing together hundreds of international university teams each year to design, build, and race high-performance formula-style cars at renowned Grand Prix circuits like Hockenheimring, Red Bull Ring, and TT Circuit Assen.

For two years, I was part of [DHBW Engineering Stuttgart e.V.](https://www.dhbw-engineering.de/), contributing across both technical engineering and team operations. As an Autonomous Systems Engineer, I worked on the vehicle's motion planning pipeline. In parallel, I was active in the Statics and Marketing team, managing financial planning and presenting in front of industry judges.

Our autonomous driving stack relied on localization and perception data from cameras and LiDAR. Within the motion planning pipeline, I worked on adapting and optimizing a beam search algorithm, refining cost functions, and implementing path smoothing via clothoids (Euler spirals) to generate smooth, continuous-curvature trajectories at racing speeds. Software development was built on ROS with mission data telemetry analyzed in Foxglove Studio, validated through extensive Software-in-the-Loop (SiL) and Hardware-in-the-Loop (HiL) testing sessions.

Our key achievements included 1st Place Overall at Formula Student Netherlands in Assen (2022), 3rd Place Overall at Formula Student Austria at the Red Bull Ring (2022), and 2nd Place Overall at Formula Student Germany at Hockenheimring (2022). The following season culminated in 3rd Place Overall at FS Germany 2023, where our team successfully finished both driverless dynamic disciplines for the first time.
Looking back, what stands out just as much as the track days is the balance between work, university, and the countless construction and late-night testing sessions in the workshop.

anecdote.headline: Monday 14:00 Exam → Spielberg → Wednesday 09:00 Exam
anecdote.text: On Monday at 14:00, I sat for a university exam. By 18:30, I set off for an 8-hour drive through the Alps to the Red Bull Ring. On Tuesday at 09:30, I held a presentation before the judges. Right after, I made the drive back to sit for my next exam on Wednesday at 09:00.
